title: Seal Kaomoji ᶘ ᵒᴥᵒᶅ: Copy & Paste Seal and Sea Lion Faces
meta_description: Copy seal kaomoji and sea lion text faces: ᶘ ᵒᴥᵒᶅ with tiny flippers, (:3 っ)っ lying on its belly, (•⩊• っ)3 and long ,◜•௰•◝,___∠ seals sliding by.
hero_tagline: Seals and sea lions typed in text: flipper faces, belly-flop seals and long sliding pups. Tap any seal to copy it.
intro: A seal kaomoji has two parts that tell it apart from a dog or bear: flippers and a round muzzle with no ears. In ᶘ ᵒᴥᵒᶅ the modifier letters ᶘ and ᶅ curl down on each side like front flippers, and ᴥ is the whiskered snout. The lying-down seals are drawn sideways: in (:3 っ)っ the :3 is the face, っ is a flipper reaching forward and a trailing 3 or ∋ is the tail fin. Longer seals stretch the body with underscores until the tail ∠ flicks up at the end. Most faces here use well-supported characters; ௰ is Tamil and may show as a box on older systems. The 🦭 seal emoji is on the animal emoji page. ಥ, 𓇼 and ௰ come from Kannada, Egyptian hieroglyphs and Tamil, so a device without those fonts shows a box in their place.

faq.q: How is a seal kaomoji different from a dog or bear one?
faq.a: Seals have no ears. A bear uses ʕ ʔ for round ears and a dog often uses ᐡ, while a seal uses ᶘ and ᶅ as flippers on each side, as in ᶘ ᵒᴥᵒᶅ.
It is a seal lying on its stomach, drawn sideways. :3 is the face, the brackets are the body and っ is a flipper. People use it for feeling lazy or flopped out.

faq.q: Is there a sea lion kaomoji?
faq.a: Text faces rarely separate the two. ᶘ ᵒᴥᵒᶅ is often used for a sea lion because the upright flippers suggest one balancing or clapping, and adding ♪ makes it bark along.
